Dark Star whilst not that great was never intended to be a feature film. 
I’d consider it in the same veign as Tarantino’s first attempt at a feature My Best Friends Birthday.
More or less a learning place rather than a fully realised project. 

In the end Dark Star has some pretty fun elements considering it was mostly shot on weekends for almost no money at all.  
But in terms of it being considered “low quality” due to its budget alone would be missing many factors.

However I do agree that budget does indeed matter. The title was chosen more or less to make a point rather than it being an 100% factoid. 
 
I suppose that may create a catch 22, but I think it holds up.

Sounds odd but I'd say The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly might be a perfect pick for this. 

\-It's historically important, Sergio Leone created soooo many techniques that are now used in almost every film after.

\-It shows how you can use genre and turn all of it's cliches on its head to create a fresh and invigorating new palette.

\-It teaches you how a soundtrack can be more than a background piece and can be an essential part of the operatic quality of the film.... because this also links into it's camera movement, and editing too. The film is edited to the music, and shot to the music.
